punchline: In Kross's research, talking to yourself by your own name made stress feel lighter.
thirty_sec: Psychologist Ethan Kross studied people on the edge of a stressful moment. One group asked themselves, "What am I going to do?" Another used their own name, as if advising a friend. The name group felt less overwhelmed and judged their own performance more evenly. One word does not fix a problem, but it can open enough distance to decide.
